item.title: John Beam’s Alleged Killer May Be Unfit to Stand Trial, Mental Health Professionals Say
item.description: Three mental health professionals evaluated the man suspected of shooting the beloved athletic director of Oakland’s Laney College and cast doubt on his mental competency.

item.title: Fremont Sergeant Bitten by Police Dog is Department’s K-9 Supervisor
item.description: Fremont Police confirmed a sergeant who accidentally shot a burglary suspect after being bitten by a police dog is the department’s K-9 Unit supervisor.

item.title: Bay Area Lawmakers Rebuke Trump Over Iran Strikes, War Authority
item.description: Bay Area members of Congress criticized President Donald Trump’s early Saturday military strikes on Iran, warning the U.S.-Israel operation risks escalation, violates congressional war powers and could lead to another prolonged Middle East conflict.

item.title: Hundreds Rally in San Francisco Against US-Israel Strikes on Iran
item.description: Demonstrators gathered at the federal building and marched through downtown San Francisco, with Iranian American and Palestinian organizers urging an end to U.S. military intervention, sanctions and expanded conflict in Iran.

item.title: San Francisco Immigration Court’s Death by a Thousand Cuts
item.description: Mission Local’s Clara-Sophia Daly explains how day to day operations — including asylum hearings — have changed.

item.title: The Eccentric Personalities Behind Sunnyside Conservatory, a 120-Year-Old Garden in San Francisco
item.description: Built in 1902 to house an eccentric inventor’s rare plant collection, preserving this building in San Francisco has been a neighborhood labor of love.

item.title: Waymo to Report on Mass Stranding Event During SF December Blackout
item.description: A San Francisco Supervisor said he will seek answers from Waymo on why many of its vehicles were disabled amid a blackout last December, and how it would prevent future outages.

item.title: How Federal Homelessness Funding Changes Could Impact Those in Need
item.description: Efforts to limit federal grant money for permanent supportive housing could lead to people losing their homes.

item.title: Newsom Expands Mental Health Court Program — and Calls Out SF for Falling Behind
item.description: Two years after the launch of CARE Court, Newsom said his office would invest hundreds of millions more dollars and aim to speed up adoption in underperforming counties like San Francisco.

item.title: It’s Expensive to Build Housing. California Lawmakers Say Factory-Built Is the Future
item.description: According to a new report from UC Berkeley’s Terner Center for Housing Innovation, manufactured housing could play a big role in bringing down the cost of construction. But first, the legislature needs to clear the red tape.
